questions.question: Kitting and assembly in warehouses mainly help in: a). Reducing storage space b). Faster order fulfillment c). Increasing production cost d). Price control / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Single Source of Truth (Centralized Database)
  • In logistics, many departments like procurement, warehousing,
  • transportation, and sales use data.
  • • ERP keeps all data in one central system
  • • Everyone sees the same updated information
  • • If stock is updated in the warehouse, the sales and
  • transport teams can immediately see it.
  • This avoids confusion like sending goods that are already
  • out of stock.

questions.question: Warehousing strategy mainly focuses on: a). Advertising products b). Efficient storage and movement of goods c). Increasing product price / [CO1] d). Market research
questions.solution_html:
• End-to-End Visibility
  • ERP gives a complete view of the entire logistics process from
  • start to finish.
  • • From ordering raw materials → storing → shipping →
  • delivery
  • • Managers can track goods at every stage
  • We can know:
  • • Where the goods are (warehouse / in transit)
  • • Delivery status
  • • Delays or bottlenecks
  • • Helps in better decision-making and faster problem-
  • solving.

questions.question: Warehousing mainly helps in: a). Production planning b). Storage of goods until consumption c). Advertising product d). Price fixation / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Process Automation
  • ERP automates repetitive logistics tasks.
  • • Automatic order processing

  • • Auto-generation of invoices and shipping documents

  • • Creates delivery order

questions.question: Explain Online Debit and Credit Card based payment systems? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain Online Debit and Credit Card based payment systems?
  • Debit card is a plastic card that provides the card holder electronic
  • access to his or her bank accounts through ATM. Debit cards are
  • Pay Now cards, the payments made using debit cards are
  • immediately debited from the card holder designated bank
  • account. VISA, MasterCard, Maestro and RuPay are the major debit
  • card brands.
  • Credit card is defined as a plastic card authorizing a purchase on
  • credit. This card enables the card holder to purchase goods, travel
  • or dine without making immediate payments. The credit card
  • issuing bank makes payment to the merchants (from the credit
  • granted to the cardholder) concern and sends statement to the
  • card holder periodically.
  • Debit Card Credit Card
  • It is a pay now product It is pay later product
  • Payment is immediately
  • debited in card holders
  • account
  • The card holder can avail
  • credit for 30 to 45 days
  • No interest charges on the use
  • of debit card
  • Interest and other charges
  • have to be paid on credit card
  • Probability of risk of fraud is
  • lower
  • Probability of risk of fraud is
  • higher
  • No risk of overspending as the
  • customer can spend what he
  • has
  • The holder tends to
  • overspending because he is
  • using the credit provided by
  • credit card issuer
  • It can be used at ATM terminal
  • to withdraw cash
  • It is commonly used to make
  • payments at POS/online. it can
  • be used in ATM with restricting
  • (like withdrawal amount, high
  • charges)
  • A bank account (Savings
  • /Current account) and
  • minimum balance should be
  • maintained
  • Minimum balance in account is
  • not compulsory in case of
  • credit cards
  • [U] / [CO4]

questions.question: Define ERP systems in Logistics. Analyze the benefits of ERP. / [CO2] [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Define ERP systems in Logistics. Analyze the benefits of ERP.
  • ERP in logistics is a software system that helps a company manage
  • and track the movement of goods from purchase to delivery in an
  • organized and efficient way.
  • An Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system is a
  • comprehensive software suite that integrates and manages an
  • [An] / [CO2]
  • organization’s core business processes across various
  • departments into a single, unified system. It provides a
  • centralized database and unified view of operations, improving
  • efficiency and enabling data-driven decision-making. ERP
  • systems also facilitate communication with external stakeholders
  • such as suppliers and customers.
  • Examples of ERP Solutions
  • SAP, Oracle ERP Cloud, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Tally ERP, Zoho
  • ERP
